issue_request: FHIR-16099 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for STU3. It asked to clarify BiologicallyDerivedProduct.collection.source from the unclear old wording about a person or entity providing the product to the approved definition: the patient or entity, such as a hospital or vendor in the case of a processed/manipulated/manufactured product, providing the product.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite commits c1f2872 and 842cb7b. The substantive BDP application is 842cb7bc8b171a6af5eaa68bc34e7e4a3817feb4, which changed the source spreadsheet short to "Who is product from" and changed the detailed definition to the approved patient-or-entity wording. The c1f2872 merge commit touched MedicinalProductIngredient only. The approved wording persisted into later generated/reworked StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: BiologicallyDerivedProduct is active in source/fhir.ini. Later applied BDP issues refined the same element family: FHIR-36696 changed the short display, FHIR-37953 rejected adding RelatedPerson and clarified patient-vs-organization source semantics, and FHIR-51939 replaced the old single collection.source with collection.sourcePatient and collection.sourceOrganization. The current StructureDefinition defines sourcePatient as the patient providing the product and sourceOrganization with the FHIR-16099 entity/hospital/vendor wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the current authoritative source already conveys the FHIR-16099 rule through the later patient and organization source elements.
